summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Dearness Allowance (DA) and related employee demands, with most factual claims being verifiable.

claims.claim: The Fourth Pay Commission recommended a DA merger when it reached 50%, which was implemented in 1987.
claims.note: Sources confirm the Fourth Pay Commission dealt with DA merger, but specific details about a 50% threshold and 1987 implementation are not consistently and clearly stated as a direct recommendation and implementation in the provided snippets. One source mentions DA being treated as pay up to an index average of 568 points before the 4th CPC.

claims.claim: The Fifth Pay Commission recommended a merger when DA crossed 50%, leading to the merger in 2004.
claims.note: The Fifth Pay Commission recommended that DA should be converted into Dearness Pay each time the CPI increases by 50% over the base index. The government issued orders on February 27, 2004, for merging 50% of DA with basic pay, effective April 1, 2004.

claims.claim: Currently, DA is revised twice a year, in January and July, based on the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) data published by the Labour Bureau.
claims.note: The CPI-IW is the official benchmark for calculating Dearness Allowance (DA) for Central and State Government employees, and DA is revised twice a year (in January and July) based on average CPI-IW values over the previous six months. The CPI-IW is compiled and published by the Labour Bureau.

claims.claim: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the government froze the Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief for central government employees and pensioners from January 1, 2020, to June 30, 2021.
claims.note: The Finance Ministry issued an order freezing DA and DR to Central government employees and pensioners at current rates till July 2021, with no arrears for the period from January 1, 2020, till June 30, 2021.

claims.claim: For Delhi, House Rent Allowance (HRA) might be 27% of Basic Pay (assuming X category city).
claims.note: Recent reports suggest that HRA for employees in X cities is paid at 27% of the basic pay. Delhi is considered an X category city.

claims.claim: The Centre recently hiked DA to 60% with effect from January 1, 2026.
claims.note: The Union Cabinet approved a 2% hike in Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief for central government employees and pensioners, raising DA/DR from 58% to 60% of basic pay from January 1, 2026.

claims.claim: DA hikes benefit approximately 50 lakh central government employees and around 65 lakh central government pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees.
